items.reason: onCreateEvent (form ngSubmit) calls router.navigate(['/my-Events']) once both createEvent and addToMyEvents succeed. That target matches the 'my-Events' child route of the '' layout route. A second trigger exists: the header is shown on /create-event (LayoutComponent renders app-header, which holds the router-outlet). Its 'My Events' dropdown link, routerLink="/my-Events" at header.component.html:29, sits under *ngIf="isLoggedIn". That condition is true on /create-event, because AuthGuardService admits only when currentUser != null, and currentUser can only be non-null after loginStatus$ has emitted true.

The only link to /register in the components shown on /create-event is the header's Sign up link, routerLink="/register" under *ngIf="!isLoggedIn" (header.component.html:20). AuthGuardService on the create-event route admits only when authService.isLoggedIn() (currentUser != null). currentUser is set only together with loginStatus true, either in setUser or in the constructor's sessionStorage path, so the header's isLoggedIn is true and the link stays hidden while the user is on the screen. Logout (header.component.ts) clears the status but immediately navigates to /login, so the link shows only for a transient moment during that navigation, which does not count. Nothing else shown there navigates to /register: CreateEventComponent navigates only to /login and /my-Events, the footer has only href="#" links, the logo points to index.html, and breadcrumbs appear only in HomeComponent.

gate.notes: I re-derived both verdicts from app-routing.module.ts, layout, header, auth.service, auth-guard.service and create-event, and the source confirms the reader on both. The create-event navigate call is at line 74, as the hint says. One reason to read the files with grep -n rather than the rtk-filtered cat -n: the filtered output numbered the lines one short in the header (19/28 instead of the real 20/29) and in create-event.component.ts (72 instead of 74).

items.reason: The literal /rules route is the top-level 'rules' route from FOLDER_RULES_ROUTES (folder-rules.module.ts:35). provideFolderRulesExtension() adds it to the root config with provideRouter. Its ROUTES providers (through ContentServiceExtensionModule and provideApplicationExtensions) are registered before provideShellRoutes(CONTENT_LAYOUT_ROUTES) in app/src/app/app.config.ts, so /rules matches it first. It renders ManageRulesSmartComponent directly in AppComponent's bare <router-outlet />, without ShellLayoutComponent, the sidenav, or the sidenav header that holds the user menu. The only trigger for /profile in the codebase is the routerLink in user-info.component.html:1. That component is reached only through the 'features.header' user menu in SidenavHeaderComponent. The manage-rules template, aca-page-layout and generic-error contain no /profile link; the only routerLink in manage-rules goes to /nodes/:id/rules. The shell-wrapped rules page is nodes/:nodeId/rules (aca-content.routes.ts:404), which is a different URL. One assumption: this relies on the route order that provideShellRoutes (from the @alfresco/adf-core/shell library, which is not installed) normally produces, with the shell route appended after earlier ROUTES providers.

The search route (aca-content.routes.ts:364) is a child of CONTENT_LAYOUT_ROUTES, which provideShellRoutes wraps in ShellLayoutComponent. The shell renders 'app.layout.sidenav', which maps to SidenavComponent. That includes app-sidenav-header, whose aca-toolbar shows the 'features.header' actions. Among them is 'app.header.more' (UserMenuComponent), a mat-menu whose 'app.header.user' item renders UserInfoComponent, which has [routerLink]="['/profile']". The sidenav is not hidden on search: hideSidenavConditions is ['/preview/'] and minimizeSidenavConditions is empty. The /profile route sits under the same shell with ViewProfileRuleGuard, which returns isLoggedIn() || isOauth(), so a signed-in user on /search can reach it.

gate.notes: I re-derived both verdicts from the source and agree with the reader on both. For /rules, Angular reads the root ROUTES multi-providers in registration order: importProvidersFrom(ContentServiceExtensionModule), which contains provideFolderRulesExtension, comes before provideShellRoutes(CONTENT_LAYOUT_ROUTES) in app.config.ts. So the flat top-level 'rules' route matches /rules before the shell's '**' route. The internals of provideShellRoutes are in the @alfresco/adf-core/shell library, which is not installed, so I assumed it appends one ROUTES entry as ADF normally does. node_modules is absent. The only extension-defined route is 'about', so nothing re-registers 'rules' under the shell.

gate.notes:
I changed 5 of the 9 verdicts, all from spurious to real. Two mechanisms explain them, and the pre-registered rules count both (whether t is reached is what matters, and a guard may stand in the way).
(1) Deep-link restore, which turns TwoFactor, NewDeviceVerification and recover-2fa into real. The UserLayout route has canActivate [deepLinkGuard(), authGuard] (src/app/oss-routing.module.ts:682). When a user who is not unlocked opens a URL there, the guard saves it in the tab's sessionStorage. When an unlocked user next enters that route, the guard calls navigateByUrl with the saved URL (src/app/auth/guards/deep-link/deep-link.guard.ts:39). Login-completing screens navigate to /vault or /settings/security/two-factor, so they can land on any authenticated route the user asked for before logging in. Only confirm-key-connector-domain, change-password, set-initial-password and login-decryption-options clear the saved URL first. If your policy treats this kind of state-driven target as unclear or as not counted, apply it to all three of these items alike, and to any other login-completing screen paired with an authenticated route.

Every AnonLayoutWrapper page shows the logo link to '/' (libs/components/src/landing-layout/landing-header.component.html:4). redirectGuard on '' (oss-routing.module.ts:130) sends unlocked users to /vault. One thing the preregistration may not cover: the Mifos Copilot panel. The shell creates it only when environment.enableCopilot is true. Its action cards call navigateByUrl with a route string sent by an external gateway.
